summary: 1944 80-foot steel fire tower in Lakewood, Ocean County, moved 300 feet in 1974; out of service July 2024 and dismantled; replacement tower built in Jackson Township.

facts.design: 80-foot all-steel Aermotor tower with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab
facts.status_note: Taken out of service in early July 2024 after the land was sold, and dismantled later that year. A replacement NJ Forest Fire Service tower has been completed on East Veterans Highway in Jackson Township.

access.note: Out of service since early July 2024. The tower no longer stands at the Massachusetts Avenue site.

events.note: Built after normal working hours by five Jersey Central Power & Light employees for $360; 80-foot tower with a 7 by 7 foot cab
April 30, 1953 blaze cut a two-mile path through more than 1,000 acres of Lakewood pineland; the alarm was sounded from the tower
Moved 300 feet because of a property dispute; remained active
Registered March 3, 2004 as US 555, NJ 14; nominated by Bob Spear
Described by the Lakewood Scoop as a vital tool in the March 2021 Airport Road wildfire
Taken out of service effective July 5, 2024 (1st Responder News); the land was sold and the lease was not renewed
Taken down after decommissioning that summer; the Lakewood Scoop showed crews dismantling it in September 2024
New NJ Forest Fire Service tower completed on East Veterans Highway, Jackson Township; construction underway through 2025; opening date not announced

corrections.why: Taken out of service in July 2024 and dismantled by September 2024; the record still shows it standing.
The Register and the Eastern lookouts page both give 80 feet, which is 24.4 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Lakewood Scoop's 2024 article says 136 feet. The Register and the Eastern page say 80 feet, and 136 feet matches the Register's elevation figure. The story uses 80 feet.
1st Responder News gives July 5, 2024 as the effective date. The Scoop reported the permanent closure in the week before its July 7 article. The story says early July 2024.
The Scoop's Jackson article calls the dismantled tower decade-old. The Register and the Eastern page date it to 1944.

notes_for_editor: Closure, dismantling and replacement all come from local news (the Lakewood Scoop, 1st Responder News). No NJFFS statement was read, and the Scoop says officials did not give a reason. A search snippet from the NJFFS Division B site says all 21 towers are in active service; that page was not read and is probably out of date. The Jackson tower's opening date is not given in the sources, so recheck before publishing. Corrections above cover the two record errors (status and height_m). The Lakewood Scoop 2024 article's 136 feet is a likely confusion with the Register's elevation.
